paragraphs: R’ Yehudah, the son of the sister of R’ Yose son of R’ Chanina.

[Ketubot 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.49b.10-11) [109b in the supplied Hebrew] and [Bava Batra 139a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.139a.19) cite Ravin’s letter about a man who died. R’ Yehudah, the son of the sister of R’ Yose son of R’ Chanina, says, “A case came through me, and they said…” etc. Hyman explains Rashbam’s statement that he was an Amora as intended to prevent the title Rabbi Yehudah from being mistaken for that of a Tanna. Hyman says Masoret HaShas on Ketubot deleted Rabbi and substituted Rav WITHOUT REASON: he was a native of Eretz Israel, where all ordained scholars were called Rabbi. Hyman cites [Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Gittin.5.3.8) for the statement in R’ Yose son of R’ Chanina’s name.[^1][^2]
He is also mentioned in Terumot, chapter 11, at the supplied locator כה״ד; the named Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud parallel is [11:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.11.4.12).

notes.text: The [printed Hyman](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=136) cites Ketubot 49b (מט:); the supplied transcription has 109b (קט:). The consulted Ketubot has Rabbi Yehudah and Bava Batra has Rav Yehudah. [Rashbam](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashbam_on_Bava_Batra.139a.19.6) calls him an Amora. Hyman argues that the Palestinian title Rabbi should stand.

In Jerusalem Gittin Rabbi Chama bar Ukva cites Rabbi Yose bar Chanina about the daughters’ marriage. In the clause about their death the nephew cites Rabbi Yose berabbi Haggai. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1702&lang=en) proposes amending the attribution there on the model of Terumot, where Rabbi Yudan speaks in the name of his maternal uncle Rabbi Yose bar Chanina.
